message:
chore(release): 0.2.105 and APK 0.2.13 candidates -- built, not shippable

Windows kProductVersion 0.2.104 -> 0.2.105, Android versionCode 11 -> 12
and versionName 0.2.12 -> 0.2.13. Same package and the same debug keystore
the deployed APK uses; no key was created or changed.

The candidates cannot check for or install an update, and that is the
correct behaviour rather than a gap. trusted_public_key_hex() is
deliberately empty and default_verifier() rejects a key of the wrong
length, so no manifest passes signature verification at all; the Android
side has empty URL and key defaults and UpdateFlow says so and does
nothing. Filling those in is an approved decision this code does not get to
make.

So this is not \"automatic updates ready for use\". What was approved is the
implementation and its isolated verification. What still needs a real
machine is unchanged: no extra UAC prompt, the client running as the
logged-on user, service registration, a real HTTPS path, an APK on a
device, anything depending on operational keys or release infrastructure,
and the backup holder -- which no longer reproduces and whose cause was
never identified.

Nothing was installed, published or pushed. 0.2.104 is untouched.
